children: Cracker Barrel's new CEO David Deno is standing by a strategy put in place by his predecessor, saying the company went through a rough patch and came out stronger. Deno joined Cracker Barrel last month, succeeding Julie Masino, who oversaw a controversial rebranding campaign that sparked widespread backlash before walking back much of the strategy. The business started showing signs of improvement before her exit. "The results of the past couple of quarters speak for themselves," Deno says during a call with analysts. "We will accomplish our objectives by relentlessly executing against the priorities we have identified." Deno says he's working to finetune the company's focus on food and customers, with plans to improve its dinner offerings and store merchandising, among other areas.(kelly.cloonan@wsj.com)
